name: Vermont
gaps: Purchase and use tax is due on the greater of the price and the J.D. Power clean trade-in value; the form does not ask the book value, so the engine taxes the price (a private sale below book value would owe more).
Safety and emissions inspection prices are set and posted by each private station; the state does not publish a fee, so the inspection is shown without an amount.
No dealer documentation fee cap was read on an official Vermont page for this release; type the dealer's fee.

tax.label: Purchase and use tax (6%)
tax.note: 6% of the price or the J.D. Power clean trade-in value, whichever is greater, minus the trade-in.

cycle.label: Clean Air Fund fee
cycle.note: Included in the $91 gas, hybrid and plug-in hybrid registration; not charged on a battery electric car.

inspection.label: Yearly safety and OBD emissions inspection (station price)
inspection.note: Due within 15 days of registering in Vermont, then once a year; each station sets and posts its price.

singular: Vermont charges a 6% purchase and use tax on the price or the J.D. Power clean trade-in value, whichever is greater [tax].
The value of a trade-in vehicle is subtracted before the 6% is applied [vd119i].
A buyer who thinks the J.D. Power value is too high can submit a Vermont Dealer Appraisal form, and DMV does not accept values from online research [vd119i].
Cars and light trucks have no maximum purchase and use tax; only trucks of 10,100 lb or more and trailers are capped at $2,486 [vd119i].
Every certificate of title costs $42, and recording a lien adds $14 [vd119i].
A one-year car registration costs $91 for a gas car, $135.50 for a plug-in hybrid and $178 for a battery electric car [fees].
The electric premium is an EV infrastructure fee of $89 a year for a battery electric car and $44.50 for a plug-in hybrid, meant for charging stations until a mileage-based fee exists [ev-fee].
The gas and plug-in hybrid registration includes a $2 Clean Air Fund fee, which is why the base fee of a battery electric car is $89 instead of $91 [fees].
Every Vermont-registered vehicle must pass a safety inspection once a year, plus an OBD emissions check when it is 16 model years old or less [inspection].
A car new to Vermont must be inspected within 15 days of registration, and each station sets and posts its own inspection price [inspection].

tax.name: Vermont DMV, Purchase and Use Tax
tax.quote: Purchase and Use Tax is due at the time of registration and/or title at the rate of 6% of the purchase price or the J. D. Power clean trade-in value, whichever is greater

vd119i.name: Vermont DMV, Registration, Tax & Title Application instructions (VD-119i, 09/2025)
vd119i.quote: All Titles (except ATV) = $42.00, ATV Titles = $27.00. Lien fee = $14.00. ... 6% of the purchase price or the JD Power value, whichever is higher, minus the value of any trade-in vehicle or any other allowable credit.

fees.name: Vermont DMV, Vehicle Registration Fees
fees.quote: Where applicable, the fees below include a $2.00 Clean Air Fund Fee and an EV Infrastructure Fee. ... Auto (car) 1 Year $91.00 $135.50 $178.00 $159.25 2 Years $167.00 $256.00 $341.00

ev-fee.name: Vermont DMV, EV Infrastructure Fee
ev-fee.quote: Plug-In Hybrid Vehicles (PHEV) One-Year ... Registration Fee $91.00 ... Infrastructure Fee $44.50 ... Battery Electric Vehicles (BEV) ... Registration Fee $89.00 $163.00 Infrastructure Fee $89.00 $178.00 Total $178.00 $341.00

inspection.name: 23 V.S.A. § 1222, Inspection of registered vehicles
inspection.quote: all motor vehicles registered in this State shall undergo a safety and visual emissions inspection once each year ... shall be inspected within 15 days following the date of its registration ... the fee shall be prominently posted
